boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Sewanee customs and recurring ceremonies, from the Honor Code to the campus guardian angel.

cards.title: Sign into the Honor Code
cards.subtitle: Matriculation tradition
cards.notes: Read the student-written Code before matriculating; signing it marks a commitment to Sewanee’s stated ideals of honor and integrity.
cards.short_summary: A student-written, student-signed pledge at the center of Sewanee community life.
cards.evidence_claim: The Honor Council chair says students matriculate into the community by signing the over-century-old Honor Code, which is written, signed, and enforced solely by students.
cards.access_notes: Applies to enrolled students during matriculation; consult the Honor Council for current procedures.

cards.title: Return the passing hello
cards.subtitle: Everyday Sewanee custom
cards.notes: When walking around the Mountain, acknowledge people you pass with a simple hello and let the small ritual set a welcoming tone.
cards.short_summary: An everyday greeting custom named by Sewanee’s Honor Council chair.
cards.evidence_claim: The Honor Council chair identifies “passing hello” as one of Sewanee’s traditions that transcends generations.
cards.access_notes: No scheduled time or formal participation requirement is stated.

cards.title: Tap for your Sewanee angel
cards.subtitle: At the campus gates
cards.notes: If you choose to follow the local custom, tap your vehicle roof on entering or leaving the gates as a nod to the guardian-angel legend.
cards.short_summary: A gate-crossing ritual tied to Sewanee’s guardian-angel folklore.
cards.evidence_claim: Sewanee’s digital history exhibition describes the enduring custom of tapping a car roof at the gates to let a guardian angel rest or travel with you.
cards.source_title: An Enduring Tradition – the Sewanee Angels
cards.access_notes: Use only when safely parked or stopped; do not distract a driver.

cards.title: Spot the academic gown in daily life
cards.subtitle: Order of the Gown custom
cards.notes: Look for the black gowns worn by Order members and faculty, and learn why Sewanee retains this visible academic distinction.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive custom in which eligible students and faculty wear gowns beyond commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says wearing the gown by students and faculty is perhaps Sewanee’s most distinctive custom; Order members have worn it as an academic badge since 1873.
cards.access_notes: Gown membership is earned under current academic eligibility requirements.

cards.title: See Gowning at Convocation
cards.subtitle: Order of the Gown induction
cards.notes: Attend the Advent Semester Convocation to witness new eligible students receive recognition in Sewanee’s formal gowning ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A ceremony honoring high-achieving students and the student-faculty relationship.
cards.evidence_claim: Sewanee calls gowning a longstanding, deeply valued tradition and states that Order of the Gown induction will take place during Advent Semester Convocation beginning in 2026–27.
cards.access_notes: The University lists the next Advent Semester Convocation for Sept. 18, 2026; verify details before attending.

cards.entity_name: Festival Service of Lessons and Carols
cards.title: Join Lessons and Carols
cards.subtitle: All Saints’ Chapel
cards.notes: Plan ahead for the annual Chapel service, where the University Choir leads carols and performs featured choral music.
cards.short_summary: A large annual worship service and signature University event.
cards.evidence_claim: All Saints’ Chapel describes its annual Lessons and Carols as a signature University event, with the University Choir leading carols and anthems.
cards.access_notes: Service dates and attendance details vary; check the Chapel’s current worship schedule.

cards.title: Browse Scholarship Sewanee
cards.subtitle: Annual undergraduate showcase
cards.notes: Set aside the day to hear student presentations and view creative work across disciplines during this campus-wide research showcase.
cards.short_summary: A daylong annual presentation of undergraduate research, scholarship, and creative work.
cards.evidence_claim: The University calls Scholarship Sewanee a beloved academic tradition and reports its 32nd annual daylong undergraduate showcase in 2025.
cards.access_notes: Annual date, presentation schedule, and public access should be confirmed with Undergraduate Research and Scholarship.

cards.title: Follow the Medieval Colloquium
cards.subtitle: Annual scholarly gathering
cards.notes: Watch for the colloquium’s program and attend eligible public sessions to encounter Sewanee’s long-running medieval-studies tradition.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding annual gathering for medieval-studies scholarship at Sewanee.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes the Sewanee Medieval Colloquium as one of medieval studies’ longest-running conferences and a valued annual tradition.
cards.access_notes: Program format and public-session availability vary by year; verify with the Medieval Studies program.

cards.title: Know the Sewanee Night history
cards.subtitle: Historic pre-football pep rally
cards.notes: Treat this as historical context: the University archive records Sewanee Night as a revived pep-rally tradition, not an orientation requirement.
cards.short_summary: A historic annual pep rally where newcomers learned cheers and campus spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Sewanee’s digital history exhibition documents Sewanee Night as an annual pre-home-football-game pep rally, especially prominent in the 1920s, and says it has been revived in recent years.
cards.source_title: Freshmen Initiated Into Sewanee Life and Spirit
cards.access_notes: The source concerns a historical, male-only period; confirm whether any current event is scheduled before planning around it.

cards.title: Mark the 50th-reunion induction
cards.subtitle: Alumni Weekend custom
cards.notes: At a 50th reunion, look for the All Saints’ ceremony that recognizes alumni for five decades of upholding Sewanee’s charge to graduates.
cards.short_summary: A special 50th-reunion ceremony welcoming alumni into the Exornati Society.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes its 50th-reunion tradition as long and storied and says reunion classes are inducted into the Exornati Society at an All Saints’ event.
cards.access_notes: This ceremony is for 50th-reunion classes; confirm the current reunion schedule with University Relations.
